chunks: Ṣafwān narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) who said:

Nothing stands between any one of you and seeing that which would bring him delight except his soul reaching here (i.e. the throat). The Angel of Death will come to him and say, ‘As for that which you used to desire in the world, it has escaped you; but as for what you used to desire of the Hereafter, you are now on the verge of it, and in front of you are the forebears of truth: the Messenger of Allah, ʿAlī and Ibrāhīm (peace be upon them all).’
ai.seo_question: What happens at the moment of death for a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Safwan ibn Yahya transmits from Abu Baseer that upon the soul reaching the throat, the Angel of Death clarifies the believer's status: worldly hopes are lost, but the Hereafter is imminent. The believer is guided by 'truthful predecessors' (suffa' sadq), specifically highlighting the Prophet Muhammad, Imam Ali, and Prophet Ibrahim, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt as intercessors and guides in the grave and beyond. This scene underscores the transition from dunya to akhira, where the believer's ultimate hope shifts from material loss to spiritual proximity to the Imams.
